paragraphs.title: Singing of Mercy and Judgment and Walking in Integrity

answers: Mercy and judgment
War and victory
Wealth and honor
easy.explanation: David says, “I will sing of mercy and judgment.”
easy.q: What does David say he will sing about?

answers: In a perfect way
In a wealthy way
In a distant way
easy.explanation: He says, “I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way.”
easy.q: In what kind of way does David say he will behave himself wisely?

answers: Within his house
At the city gate
In a foreign land
easy.explanation: David says, “I will walk within my house with a perfect heart.”
easy.q: Where does David say he will walk with a perfect heart?

answers: When He will come unto him
When He will give him riches
When He will defeat his enemies
medium.explanation: David asks, “O when wilt thou come unto me?”
medium.q: What does David ask the LORD?

answers: A way of integrity and a wholehearted heart
A powerful army
A beautiful house
medium.explanation: The passage connects “perfect” with David’s conduct and the condition of his heart.
medium.q: What does the word “perfect” describe in these verses?

answers: David first speaks of singing and then describes how he will live
David first describes a battle and then asks for a house
David first speaks of lies and then praises wealth
medium.explanation: David begins with a song about mercy and judgment and then describes his wise and upright conduct.
medium.q: How are the two verses connected?

answers: His integrity is meant to govern both his public conduct and private life
He wants to leave his house
His house is a place of warfare
challenge.explanation: David speaks of behaving wisely in his way and walking with a perfect heart within his house.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David mentioning both his way and his house?

answers: Both concern righteous conduct before God
Both describe material wealth
Both concern enemies and battles
challenge.explanation: David’s song about mercy and judgment is followed by his commitment to live uprightly.
challenge.q: What connection exists between mercy and judgment and a perfect way?

answers: Singing, asking when the LORD will come, and declaring integrity at home
Describing enemies, fleeing, and returning home
Speaking of lies, punishment, and wealth
challenge.explanation: The verses move from singing, to a question for the LORD, to a declaration about David’s conduct.
challenge.q: What is the order of ideas in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Rejecting Evil and the Crooked Heart

answers: A wicked thing
A perfect way
The faithful of the land
easy.explanation: David says, “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.”
easy.q: What does David say he will not set before his eyes?

answers: The work of them that turn aside
Mercy
Faithfulness
easy.explanation: He says, “I hate the work of them that turn aside.”

answers: A froward heart
A perfect heart
A faithful heart
easy.explanation: David says, “A froward heart shall depart from me.”
easy.q: What kind of heart shall depart from David?

answers: Something evil or morally corrupt
Something merciful
Something wise and faithful
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to something wrong that David refuses to place before his eyes.
medium.q: What does “a wicked thing” mean in this passage?

answers: He does not want evil to cling to him
He wants to study evil more closely
He wants to sing about wickedness
medium.explanation: David says of the work of those who turn aside, “it shall not cleave to me.”
medium.q: Why does David refuse to set wickedness before his eyes?

answers: David seeks distance from both inward corruption and wicked people
David wants to learn from both
David describes both as examples of mercy
medium.explanation: David says that a froward heart shall depart from him and that he will not know a wicked person.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the froward heart and the wicked person?

answers: David guards both what he sees and his inner character
David is concerned only with outward appearance
David ignores inward evil
challenge.explanation: The verses address both what David places before his eyes and the condition of his heart.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from the eyes to the heart?

answers: David refuses fellowship or close association with wickedness
David wants to learn every kind of evil
David says that wickedness is a perfect way
challenge.explanation: In context, David is declaring that he will not accept or associate with a wicked person.
challenge.q: What does “I will not know a wicked person” mean in context?

answers: He rejects wickedness before his eyes, hates corrupt works, and removes the froward heart
He seeks wickedness, welcomes it, and praises those who turn aside
He sings about evil and chooses wicked companions
challenge.explanation: The verses present a consistent rejection of outward evil, corrupt actions, and inward crookedness.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes David’s position?

paragraphs.title: Choosing Trustworthy People and Rejecting Deceit

answers: The one who secretly slanders his neighbour
The faithful of the land
The one who walks in a perfect way
easy.explanation: David says, “Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off.”
easy.q: Whom does David say he will cut off?

answers: The faithful of the land
Those who tell lies
Those who work deceit
easy.explanation: David says, “Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land.”
easy.q: Whose eyes shall be upon David’s attention?

answers: The one who works deceit
The one who walks in a perfect way
The faithful servant
easy.explanation: David says, “He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house.”
easy.q: Who shall not dwell within David’s house?

answers: Secretly speaks evil against another person
Publicly praises a faithful neighbor
Wisely instructs a servant
medium.explanation: To slander privily is to speak harmful accusations secretly against one’s neighbor.

answers: They walk in a perfect way
They tell lies skillfully
They have a high and proud look
medium.explanation: David says that the one who walks in a perfect way “shall serve me.”
medium.q: Why does David favor the faithful of the land?

answers: Deceitful people have no place within David’s house
All deceivers are welcomed into the house
David leaves his house because of the faithful
medium.explanation: The passage says that the one who works deceit shall not dwell within David’s house.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between deceit and the household?

answers: David chooses people according to faithfulness and integrity rather than deceit
David prefers lies to uprightness
David makes no distinction between them
challenge.explanation: David watches for the faithful but refuses those who work deceit or tell lies.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between the faithful and those who tell lies?

answers: They oppose the moral character David seeks around him
They all walk in a perfect way
They are all faithful servants
challenge.explanation: David rejects slander, pride, deceit, and lies as inconsistent with his household.
challenge.q: What common quality makes the slanderer, the proud person, and the liar unsuitable for David’s household?

answers: He rejects slander and pride, chooses the faithful, and excludes deceit and lies
He welcomes liars, rejects the faithful, and honors the proud
He chooses the proud, welcomes deceit, and rejects those who walk perfectly
challenge.explanation: The passage first identifies those David rejects, then names the faithful he welcomes, and finally excludes deceitful and lying people.
challenge.q: What is the order of David’s decisions in this passage?

answers: Early
At midnight
At the end of the year
easy.explanation: David says, “I will early destroy all the wicked of the land.”
easy.q: When does David say he will act?

answers: All the wicked of the land
The faithful of the land
Those who walk in a perfect way
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will early destroy all the wicked of the land.”
easy.q: Whom does David say he will destroy?

answers: The city of the LORD
His own house
A distant nation
easy.explanation: David says he will cut off all wicked doers “from the city of the LORD.”
easy.q: From where does David seek to cut off wicked doers?

answers: Prompt or repeated action at the beginning of the day
An action taken only once at night
An action delayed until the end of the year
medium.explanation: The word emphasizes David’s readiness to act early against wickedness.
medium.q: What does “early” emphasize in this verse?

answers: Both refer to people who practice evil
One refers to the faithful and the other to the perfect
One refers to mercy and the other to judgment
medium.explanation: Both expressions describe people whose actions are wicked.
medium.q: What is the relationship between “the wicked of the land” and “wicked doers”?

answers: It shows that the action is directed against every wicked doer
It limits the action to one person
It cancels the action
medium.explanation: The word “all” makes the scope of David’s intended action comprehensive.
medium.q: What does the word “all” add to David’s statement?

answers: He describes a determined and ongoing policy rather than a single impulsive act
He intends to act only once
He is merely singing without making a decision
challenge.explanation: The timing and firm language show David’s readiness to deal consistently with wickedness.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s early action against the wicked?

answers: It presents the city as a place that should be kept free from wicked doers
It presents the city as a place devoted to lies
It shows that the city has no connection with moral conduct
challenge.explanation: David seeks to remove wicked doers from the city associated with the LORD.
challenge.q: What does mentioning “the city of the LORD” add to the verse?

answers: It turns David’s rejection of evil into a practical and determined action
It cancels the importance of integrity and faithfulness
It replaces justice with material prosperity
challenge.explanation: After rejecting wickedness and choosing faithful people, David describes removing evildoers from the LORD’s city.
challenge.q: How does verse 8 continue the earlier ideas of the psalm?
